patch.value: GH-1184: scalar merge conflict ordering ignores recency and requested preference

On pm 2026.9.3, same-field scalar conflicts converge by lexicographic stable_value_order. This preserves direction independence but can retain an older status or priority solely because its serialized spelling sorts first, while --prefer ours|theirs is recorded yet does not affect the result. The report proposes a direction-independent recency key with an explicit deterministic tie-break, or a truthful narrowing of the --prefer contract.

Both merge directions converge to the same scalar value; the ordering key is declared and uses meaningful recorded evidence rather than spelling; --prefer behavior and exclusions are machine-readable and match help; status and priority regressions cover older/newer writes, equal timestamps, both directions, and both preference values; receipts remain truthful and privacy-safe
pm-cli 2026.9.3; Node 26.5.0; Linux; fresh merge-driver install

Create one item, diverge two branches, update the same scalar at different timestamps, then merge in both directions with default, --prefer ours, and --prefer theirs; observe the same lexicographically smaller value retained.

A documented deterministic policy preserves direction-independent convergence while choosing by meaningful recorded evidence, and any advertised preference control either affects its declared class or explicitly excludes it.
stable_value_order retains lexicographically smaller statuses and numeric values independent of write time, merge direction, and --prefer.
